data.title: koan v1: a reproducible random draw over hand-curated lists
data.description:
A single Go binary, usable on any project, that draws seeded random values from
hand-curated bags and renders them into a template, to push a language model out of
the centre of its distribution. The contract, the exit table and the verbs are in
project/2026-09-05-koan-vision-and-plan.md; this tree implements that document and
nothing beyond it. The list of what v1 deliberately leaves out is in the same document.

data.title: Bags: resolve, load and validate .txt and .csv
data.description:
The library's bag loader. A slot name resolves to `<name>.txt` then `<name>.csv`
in the bags directory, exact and case-sensitive. Both present is an error naming
both paths. `.txt` is a line per value, verbatim, nothing parsed. `.csv` is RFC 4180
via encoding/csv with ragged rows allowed and the first column as the value. Both
skip `#` lines and blanks and trim values. Duplicates are kept, because a duplicate
is a weight. Missing bag, empty bag, empty first cell and CSV parse error are typed
errors carrying the path and line so the CLI can map each to exit 4 and a remedy.

Tests first, all red: each format, comments, weights, ambiguity, every error, and
the unquoted-comma case in `.csv` asserted as the documented truncation so it is
intended rather than discovered.

criteria.label: Every error type is a distinct Go type carrying path and, where there is one, line
An unquoted comma in a .csv value is covered by a test that documents the truncation
A .txt value containing commas and quotes loads verbatim
adjective.txt beside adjective.csv is refused naming both paths

data.title: Templates: parse slots and render
data.description:
Parse a template into literal runs and `{slot}` names matching [A-Za-z0-9_.-]+,
preserving order of first appearance and recording whether the template spans more
than one line. Render from a map of slot to value; a repeated slot repeats the value.
No escape syntax: unmatched braces are literal. Unbound slots are the draw's concern,
but the parser exposes the ordered slot list so lint and draw share it.

criteria.label: Slot order is order of first appearance and a repeated slot appears once in the list
A template with a newline reports multi-line
Braces that do not form a slot render literally

data.title: Draw: seeded stream, -n and without-replacement
data.description:
Given bags, a template, a seed and n, produce n draws from one PCG stream seeded
(seed, 0), pulling slots in template order, and never repeating a value within a bag
across the n draws of one invocation. The n+1th draw of a run equals the extra draw
of a longer run with the same seed. When a bag cannot supply a further distinct
value, return a typed exhaustion error naming the bag, the pool size and how many
were needed, so the CLI can map it to exit 3 with the remedy. Bind unbound slots to
a typed error for exit 4.

criteria.label: The same seed and bags produce byte-identical draws across runs
-n 5 begins with the three draws of -n 3 under the same seed
A bag of two values with -n 3 fails with the exhaustion error, not a repeat
A slot with no bag fails naming the slot and both paths tried

data.title: Used directory: exclude before, record after
data.description:
`--used <dir>` reads the directory as a bags directory and subtracts every value
found in `<name>.txt` or `<name>.csv` from the matching pool, by value, however many
times the bag repeats it. After a fully successful run it appends each drawn value to
`<dir>/<name>.txt`, creating the directory and files as needed; nothing is written if
any draw failed. Failure to create or write maps to exit 5. No locking in v1, noted in
the plan doc's not-in-v1 list.

criteria.label: A value present in used/<bag>.txt is never drawn
After a run of -n 3 each drawn value appears once in the used file
A run that fails on exhaustion writes nothing
Exclusion of a weighted value removes every copy

data.title: CLI: root draw, flags, output modes and exit codes
data.description:
The Cobra adapter. Bare `koan` prints the primer. `koan <template>` draws, with
`--bags` defaulting to the template's directory (cwd for `-`), `--used`, `--seed`,
`-n` and `--json`. stderr always carries `seed=N`. Plain output is one line per draw
and refuses a multi-line template with a message naming `--json`. `--json` is JSON
Lines with seed, i, template, slots and text per line. Every library error maps to
the plan doc's exit table with a message that names the path, what happened and the
next command. Tests drive the built binary on fixture copies in a temp dir and assert
bytes and exit codes; every error path has a test that reads its remedy.

criteria.label: Bare koan exits 0 with the primer and no file, network or state
Golden tests pin plain and JSONL output for a fixed seed
Each row of the exit table has a binary test producing that code
The multi-line-without-json error names --json

data.title: Read verbs: bags, lint, recipes, schema and per-verb help
data.description:
`koan bags [dir] [--used dir]` prints one row per bag with name, format, values,
used, remaining and a problem flag, and `--json` for the same. `koan lint <template>…`
reports everything draw would refuse, for every template given, without drawing, and
exits 1 on a finding. `koan recipes` routes goals to commands. `koan schema` prints
the template grammar, the JSONL shape and the exit table. Every verb's `--help`
carries one worked example. The acceptance test is an agent reading only the tool's
own output: run `koan`, then `koan --help`, then each verb's help, and check that the
quick start in the README adds nothing the help did not already say.

criteria.label: koan bags on the examples directory prints one row per bag with counts
koan lint exits 1 on a template with an unbound slot and 0 on a clean one
Every verb's --help includes a worked example
recipes and schema run with no arguments and no files present

data.text:
Settled before dispatch (2026-09-05, Ben agreed to the assessment):

- Algorithm: for each slot in template order, pick `IntN(len(remaining))` from the bag's remaining pool and remove the chosen value. Prefix-stable by construction, so `-n 5` extends `-n 3`.
- Weights under without-replacement: drawing a weighted value removes every copy of that value from the pool for the rest of the run, so exhaustion counts distinct values. This mirrors used exclusion, which is by value.
- Old seeds from the original script do not reproduce old koans (it drew with replacement). Green-field; the seed-412 example in the plan is illustrative, not a fixture.

Settled before dispatch (2026-09-05): the used directory is read as a bags directory, so `<name>.csv` there is honoured on exclusion. Recording appends to whichever file already exists for the bag, writing through encoding/csv when it is `.csv` so commas quote; only a bag with no used file yet gets a fresh `<name>.txt`. This avoids manufacturing the ambiguous .txt/.csv pair on the next run.

Template parser and renderer landed on wt/template as `template.go` + `template_test.go`
(root package `koan`, no new dependency; stdlib `regexp` only).

API as consumed by draw and the CLI:

    func ParseTemplate(text string) *Template          // cannot fail
    func ReadTemplate(r io.Reader) (*Template, error)
    func (*Template) Source() string
    func (*Template) Slots() []string                  // fresh copy, first appearance, each once
    func (*Template) MultiLine() bool
    func (*Template) Render(map[string]string) (string, error)
    type MissingValueError struct{ Slot string }

DECISION — trailing newlines. `ParseTemplate` applies `strings.TrimRight(text, "\r\n")` to the
source before parsing. A template file normally ends in `\n`, and the plan requires a single-line
template for plain output; without the trim every ordinary one-line template file would report
multi-line and be rejected. Consequences, all covered by tests: `Source()` returns the trimmed
text, so `Render` emits no trailing newline and the caller owns the line ending; several trailing
newlines and `\r\n` are stripped equally; a template that is only `"\n"` parses as empty and
single-line; a newline anywhere else makes `MultiLine()` true and is preserved verbatim in the
rendered output.

DECISION — a slot is matched by one compiled regexp, `\{[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+\}`, scanned left to
right. That yields the plan's literal-brace behaviour without a hand-written scanner: `{}` and
`{a b}` are literal because the name run is empty or the run is not followed by `}`; `{{a}}` is a
literal `{`, the slot `a`, and a literal `}` because no match starts at index 0 but one starts at
index 1; `{a{b}` is literal `{a` plus the slot `b`. Adjacent slots `{a}{b}` are two slots.

DECISION — `Render` is fail-closed. A slot with no key in the values map returns
`*MissingValueError{Slot}` and an empty string, never a partial render, per the plan's "a template
can never render short". An entry present with an empty value renders empty and is not an error;
values with no matching slot are ignored.

Criteria coverage (left unmarked for whoever closes the leaf):
- hCQ order of first appearance, repeat listed once — TestParseTemplateSlotsAreInOrderOfFirstAppearance, TestRenderRepeatsARepeatedSlot
- tth newline reports multi-line — TestParseTemplateReportsAnInteriorNewlineAsMultiLine, TestParseTemplateStripsTrailingNewlines, TestParseTemplateReportsALoneNewlineAsSingleLine
- Ozv braces that do not form a slot render literally — TestParseTemplateTreatsMalformedBracesAsLiteralText (8 subtests)

TDD note, honestly: tests were written first and failed at compile, then failed individually
against a zero-value stub — except `TestParseTemplateEmpty` and
`TestParseTemplateReportsALoneNewlineAsSingleLine`, which were green against the stub because
their expected results (empty source, no slots, not multi-line, empty render) are exactly the zero
values. They are real cases worth keeping, but no stub can make them red; they are the two tests in
this file that the red phase did not exercise.

Verified with the sandbox disabled from the worktree root: `go test ./...` ok (28 test cases pass),
`go vet ./...`, `gofmt -l .` (silent), `go fix ./...`, `go build ./...` all clean.

A template with a newline reports multi-line

data.note: Merged to main as f381cb1 after reading the full diff. 127-line template.go on a single compiled regexp; 28 test cases. Two flags from the agent worth carrying forward: (1) `{.}`, `{-}` and `{...}` are valid slot names under the plan's character class, so lint should say plainly that no such bag exists rather than choke; (2) TrimRight on "\r\n" also strips bare trailing carriage returns, which is intended.

data.text:
Bag loader landed on wt/bags: `bag.go` (289 lines), `bag_errors.go` (123), `bag_test.go` (26 tests, all
passing), fixtures under `testdata/bags{,-ambiguous,-broken,-crlf,-multiline}/`. Strict red/green: the
test file was written first and failed to compile on every symbol.

Two decisions the plan did not settle, both load-bearing for the leaves that follow:

1. **Resolution reads the directory; it never stats a path.** macOS APFS is case-insensitive by default,
   so `os.Stat("bags/Adjective.txt")` happily answers for `adjective.txt` and the plan's "exact and
   case-sensitive, no plural or singular guessing" would be false on the machine we develop on. `bagFiles`
   builds a set from `os.ReadDir` and matches `name+".txt"` exactly, which also makes the ambiguity check
   exact and makes a path separator in a name unresolvable rather than a traversal. The `used` leaf should
   do the same when it reads `<dir>/<bag>.txt`.

2. **`#` comments in `.csv` are masked before `encoding/csv` sees them, quote-aware, preserving line
   numbers.** The dropped line is replaced by an empty line rather than removed, so `EmptyValueError` and
   `CSVError` report the author's real line number (a mutation that removed the line instead shifted
   `blankcell.csv` from line 3 to line 2 — the tests catch it). The mask tracks quote parity so a line
   opening with `#` inside a multi-line RFC 4180 quoted field stays part of the value; without that it was
   silently corrupting the value, which is the failure mode the plan's "a bag can never hold a hole" is
   about. `csv.Reader.Comment` was not usable: it only honours a `#` in column 1, and the contract is
   "first non-blank character".

Two notes for the CLI leaf. The plan's ".txt then .csv" resolution *order* is not observable, because a
name backed by both is an error rather than a precedence — the only testable claims are that each format
resolves on its own and that a pair is refused. And every error message keeps its remedy about the file
(`remove one of them`, `quote the value or delete the row`, `create one of them`); the command-level
remedy and the exit code are the CLI's to add.

The API is exactly as briefed, so `draw`, `lint` and `bags` should fit without edits: `Format`/`FormatTxt`
/`FormatCSV`, `Bag`, `LoadBag`, `LoadBags` (joins in names order, keeps the bags that loaded, loads a
repeated name once), `Listed`, `ListBags`, and `MissingBagError`, `AmbiguousBagError`, `EmptyBagError`,
`EmptyValueError`, `CSVError`, `ReadError` — all pointer types, `CSVError` and `ReadError` unwrapping.

Verified with `go fix ./...`, `gofmt -l .`, `go vet ./...`, `go test ./...` from the worktree root.

data.note: Merged to main as 9f556ba after reading the full diff (bag.go, bag_errors.go, bag_test.go, five fixture dirs). Accepted both of the agent's design calls: directory-entry matching instead of stat so case-sensitivity holds on APFS, and quote-aware comment masking that preserves line numbers. One doc comment reworded on LoadBag to drop the unobservable .txt-then-.csv order. Carry forward to the used leaf: it reads its directory as a bags directory, so it inherits the same case-sensitive resolution for free via LoadBags.

data.text:
API fixed before dispatch (2026-09-05), so the CLI leaf can be briefed against it:

- `type Koan struct { Seed uint64 "json:seed"; Index int "json:i"; Template string "json:template"; Slots map[string]string "json:slots"; Text string "json:text" }` — the one wire struct both the library and the CLI use for JSONL. Slots marshal in encoding/json's alphabetical key order; template order would need a custom marshaller and JSON object order carries no meaning.
- `type Request struct { Template *Template; Name string; Bags map[string]*Bag; Seed uint64; Count int }`; `func Draw(req Request) ([]Koan, error)`.
- Stream: `rand.New(rand.NewPCG(seed, 0))`; per draw, per slot in template order, `IntN(len(remaining))` then remove every copy of the chosen value from that bag's remaining pool. Each draw consumes exactly len(slots) numbers, so prefixes are stable.
- `*ExhaustedError{Name, Path string; Available, Needed int}` when a pool is empty; `*UnboundSlotError{Slot string}` when a slot has no bag in the map (a guard; the CLI reaches MissingBagError first via LoadBags(dir, tmpl.Slots())).
- Draw and used are carried by one agent, since used's exclusion and recording are defined in terms of Draw's pool and Koan.

API fixed before dispatch (2026-09-05):

- `func LoadUsed(dir string, names []string) (map[string]*Bag, error)` — reads dir as a bags directory (so it inherits exact, case-sensitive resolution); a missing directory, a missing used file or an empty one means nothing used; every other bag error propagates.
- `func Exclude(bags, used map[string]*Bag) map[string]*Bag` — fresh bags with every value present in used removed, every copy, by exact value.
- `func Record(dir string, koans []Koan) error` — appends each koan's values to `<dir>/<name>.txt`, or `<name>.csv` when that is the file already there (through encoding/csv so commas quote), creating the directory; failures are `*RecordError{Path string; Err error}` for exit 5.
- Draw and used are carried by one agent.

Draw implemented in draw.go, tested in draw_test.go (red first: the suite failed to compile on the whole test file, then went green).

Built exactly to the fixed API: Koan, Request, Draw, *ExhaustedError, *UnboundSlotError.

Decisions taken inside the brief:

- Two validation passes, not one interleaved pass. Every slot is checked for a bag first (exit-4 territory), then every bag is checked for Count distinct values (exit-3). Interleaving would report exhaustion for slot a when slot b is unbound, which inverts the exit codes: a load failure should always beat a pool failure.
- distinctCount builds a set; withoutValue is slices.DeleteFunc over a clone of Bag.Values, so the caller's bags are untouched (pinned by TestDrawDoesNotMutateBags).
- Render's *MissingValueError is propagated rather than ignored. It cannot fire — Slots() covers every part of kind partSlot — but swallowing it would hide a template bug.
- ExhaustedError message: "bag adjective (testdata/bags/adjective.txt) has 2 distinct values, 3 draws need 3", verbatim from the brief so the CLI leaf's remedy composes. UnboundSlotError: "no bag bound to slot {muse}", matching MissingValueError's "{slot}" convention.

The slot-order test was mutation-checked: adding slices.Sort(slots) to Draw makes TestDrawSlotOrderFollowsTemplate fail, so it really pins that template order reaches the stream rather than passing vacuously.

Used directory implemented in used.go, tested in used_test.go (red first: the suite failed to compile on the whole test file, then went green). LoadUsed, Exclude, Record, *RecordError, exactly the fixed API.

Two places the brief could not be followed literally, both resolved in the code:

1. The trailing-newline guard cannot use the append handle. The brief says open with O_APPEND|O_CREATE|O_WRONLY and apply the same newline guard; a write-only fd cannot be read, so ReadAt on it fails with EBADF. lacksFinalNewline() stats the path and, only when it is non-empty, opens a short read-only handle to read the last byte, before the append handle is opened. It reads one byte, not the file, since a used file grows without bound.

2. LoadUsed calls bagFiles(dir) once and then loadResolved per name, rather than LoadBag per name. Same package, same resolution, but one directory read instead of N — and an unreadable used directory yields one *ReadError instead of N identical ones. *MissingBagError and *EmptyBagError are swallowed; everything else is collected and joined, the shape LoadBags already uses.

Other decisions:

- Record picks .txt when it exists, else .csv when that exists, else .txt. That is the brief's rule and its "if both exist, append to .txt" fallback in one precedence, with no second ambiguity check — the loader owns that rule.
- The CSV newline guard writes a raw "\n" to the fd before any csv.Writer record is buffered, so the ordering is right despite the Writer's buffering. Pinned for both formats by TestRecordClosesAnUnterminatedFile.
- Handles are opened lazily per bag and kept open for the whole run, closed by an explicit loop with a deferred close as the safety net; close() is idempotent.
- Not atomic: if a write fails midway, the values already appended stay. Making a run's record all-or-nothing wants a temp file and a rename per bag, which is next to the locking question already parked in backlog.md. Worth a backlog line if the integrator agrees.

Which test pins which criterion:
- dBU (a used value is never drawn) — TestUsedRoundTrip, the full loop: draw, Record, LoadUsed, Exclude, draw again under seed 412, assert no value recurs.
- 1qM (each drawn value appears once after -n 3) — TestRecordAppendsInKoanOrder, which also pins the order.
- C6V (a failed run writes nothing) — TestRecordOfNothingWritesNothing: Draw's exhaustion returns nil koans, and Record of nothing does not even create the directory.
- RsB (exclusion of a weighted value removes every copy) — TestExcludeRemovesEveryCopy.

The exclusion tests were mutation-checked: disabling the used lookup inside Exclude fails TestExcludeRemovesEveryCopy, TestExcludeCanEmptyABag and TestUsedRoundTrip, so none of them passes vacuously.

Note for whoever edits the plan: project/2026-09-05-koan-vision-and-plan.md, "Invocation", still describes --used as reading and appending to "<dir>/<bag>.txt" only. The settled decision on this leaf is that the used directory is read as a bags directory, so <bag>.csv is honoured on exclusion and appended to when it is the file already there. The plan text is stale on that point.

Criteria: enY, o5d and rUa marked passed, each pinned by a named test in draw_test.go — enY by TestDrawDeterministic (two draws under seed 412 marshal to identical bytes), o5d by TestDrawPrefixStable (-n 3 equals the first three of -n 5 under seed 99), rUa by TestDrawExhausted (a bag of two values with -n 3 returns *ExhaustedError{Available:2, Needed:3} and no koans).

geT left pending on purpose. Its library half is done — TestDrawUnboundSlot pins *UnboundSlotError naming the slot — but "and both paths tried" belongs to *MissingBagError, which is what the CLI actually meets, since it loads bags for exactly Template.Slots(). UnboundSlotError is the guard behind it and has no paths to name. The criterion is only observable end to end once the CLI leaf wires LoadBags to the template's slots, so whoever closes it should check it there.

Draw's other pinned behaviours, for the record: TestDrawNoRepeatWithinBag, TestDrawWeightRemovesEveryCopy (20 seeds), TestDrawExhaustedCountsDistinct, TestDrawExhaustedNamesFirstSlot, TestDrawRepeatedSlot, TestDrawSlotOrderFollowsTemplate, TestDrawKoanFields, TestKoanJSONKeys, TestDrawCountBelowOne, TestDrawNoSlots, TestDrawDoesNotMutateBags.

data.text: Settled before dispatch (2026-09-05): the CLI composes the library as ReadTemplate → LoadBags(dir, tmpl.Slots()) → LoadUsed/Exclude when --used → Draw → print → Record when --used. Koan.Template is the template path as typed, "-" for stdin. --bags defaults to the template's directory, cwd for stdin. Exit codes per the plan's table; every library error type maps to one code and a message ending in the next command.

Example bags written to examples/art-director/ on 2026-09-05 while the CLI leaf was in flight: adjective.csv (51), quality.csv (47), muse.csv (31) with a `# name,comment` header, constraint.txt (46, ten with commas) and art-director.txt. Vocabulary copied verbatim from the client project's script, including one misspelt adjective, because the bags are hand-curated and not mine to edit. Header comments are rewritten; nothing names the client. The README quick start waits for the binary.

Built the Cobra adapter in the wt/cli worktree: cmd/koan/{main,root,output,errors,help}.go plus cli_test.go and errors_test.go, all driving the built binary on copies of testdata in a temp dir.

Shape: main.go is 11 lines (os.Exit(run(...))). root.go holds the draw pipeline — ReadTemplate -> LoadBags(bagsDirFor(flag,path), tmpl.Slots()) -> LoadUsed/Exclude -> Draw -> seed=N to stderr -> stdout -> Record. errors.go owns the exit table (typed exitCode constants) and turns every library error into "koan: <library message>" plus one "remedy: <next command>" line; a joined LoadBags error is flattened to one koan: line per leaf with a single shared remedy. output.go has the plain and JSONL writers.

Decisions worth knowing:
- -n is registered as IntVarP(&count, "count", "n", 1, ...), so -n 3 works and the long form is --count. Naming the flag "n" with shorthand "n" would print "-n, --n int" in help.
- The root command MUST set Args explicitly. Cobra's default legacyArgs rejects any unknown first positional on a root that has subcommands with `unknown command "x" for "koan"`; with our own Args func, `koan template.txt` reaches RunE. A template literally named bags is still ./bags, and root --help says so.
- Bare `koan` (no args AND cmd.Flags().NFlag() == 0) calls cmd.Help(), so `koan` and `koan --help` are byte-identical. Args with flags but no template is exit 2, not the primer.
- seed=N is printed only after Draw returns successfully, so a failed run leaves nothing but its error on stderr. Pinned by wantNoSeedLine on the -n, multi-line, exhaustion and template-read failures.
- Exit 5 is reachable only when the used directory reads but does not write: a path whose parent is a regular file fails in LoadUsed first (exit 4, per the contract). TestRecordFailureIsFive uses a 0555 directory; TestUnreadableUsedDirectoryIsFour covers the other.
- JSONL is written with a json.Encoder with SetEscapeHTML(false) rather than json.Marshal, so an ampersand or an angle bracket in prose stays readable; the values are identical.

Goldens (seed 412 over testdata/bags, template testdata/cli/koan.txt) were pinned after the first green run — the accepted exception. My hand-written guesses were wrong, which is the point of pinning from the binary.

Fixtures added under testdata/cli/: koan.txt (four slots), multi.txt, unbound.txt, repeat.txt, slotless.txt, solo.txt, broken.txt, and round/ (animal.txt, verb.txt, round.txt) — six distinct values per bag so -n 5 and the --used tests have room.

Built the four read/help verbs in the wt/cli worktree: cmd/koan/bags.go, cmd/koan/lint.go and the static text in cmd/koan/help.go, with read_test.go driving the binary.

koan bags [dir] [--used dir] [--json]
- One bagRow struct backs both shapes, so the plain columns and the JSON keys cannot drift. Plain is a header plus one text/tabwriter row: NAME FORMAT VALUES USED REMAINING PROBLEM, VALUES being the DISTINCT count (a duplicated line is a weight, not a second draw). A broken bag carries "-" in all three numeric columns and its message in PROBLEM; a sound bag carries "-" in PROBLEM.
- Exit 0 even with broken bags (it is a read; lint is the assertion). Exit 4 only when the directory itself cannot be read — and, a judgement call beyond the brief, when the --used directory will not load: reporting 0 used for a used directory koan could not read would be a plausible wrong answer. TestBagsBrokenUsedDirectoryIsFour pins it.
- The plain golden for testdata/bags is pinned in read_test.go; tabwriter gives the same bytes in a pipe and a terminal.

koan lint <template>... [--bags dir] [--used dir]
- Per template: an unreadable template is a finding like any other (so lint is only ever 0, 1 or 2), then every LoadBags error via the join, then every LoadUsed error, then after Exclude any bag with zero distinct values left, reported as the koan.ExhaustedError the draw would give with Needed 1. One line per finding as "<template>: <message>"; a clean template prints "<template>: ok". A multi-line template is not a finding.

koan recipes / koan schema
- Static text, exit 0, no files needed. recipes routes ten goals to commands, including the .txt-vs-.csv rule for writing a new bag and the stdin form. schema carries the slot regex, both bag formats with the unquoted-comma trap, the JSONL shape with a worked line and a key gloss, the seed=N line, the used-directory rule with the reproducibility caveat, and the exit table.
- Both README "Two things to know" items (quote commas in .csv, reproduce without --used) are in koan schema, so the acceptance test holds: the help says everything the README's prose does.

Every verb has a cobra Example block; each --help runs in an empty directory (TestEveryVerbHelpCarriesAnExample). The primer groups the verbs by role with cobra command groups plus an explicit "The verbs, by role" block in the Long text, because the act verb is the root and has no group heading of its own.
